description:
## Observations (main 0.7.2, 3-node ../bedrock_ex harness, loopback, MinIO)

1. With c1 kill -9'd and c2/c3 alive (a 2-of-3 quorum), leadership alternated between c2 and c3 roughly once per second for ~40s (epochs 5 -> 26), each new leader launching a Director that stalled on :unable_to_meet_log_quorum, then settled at term 26 with healthy 100ms heartbeats. It flapped again (epochs 27 -> 47) when c1 briefly connected and crashed during boot (bedrock-awj.1 startup race, fixed on develop).
2. Contrast: an earlier kill of c2 left c1 leading stably for 45s under the same stall.
3. One `:undecided` leadership change fired on all three nodes at once (15:05:54) with every node healthy and idle, ~66s after boot. It did not reproduce on a fresh cluster (idle baseline, normal RPCs, killed hidden control nodes). That election handed leadership to a follower with a stale prior_core_state and wiped the cluster (see the prior_core_state P0 ticket).

## Unknown

Mechanism. Candidates to falsify: coordinator process blocked (synchronous work on leadership change / director cleanup / durable writes) missing heartbeat or election timers; competing Directors of different epochs locking each other's logs; nodeup/nodedown of a crash-looping peer resetting raft state; election timeout/heartbeat constants too tight for a BEAM under load.

## Expected

With a quorum of healthy coordinators and no partitions, leadership is stable. A dead or crash-looping minority must not cause elections. Spike first — prove the mechanism with a deterministic repro before any fix.

comments.text:
Cross-reference: bedrock-wyo looks like the same root cause observed from the other end.

The chaos-harness baseline (bedrock-hve.5, :peer-based 3-node cluster in ExUnit, no faults injected) hits a permanent stuck state in ~2% of cluster starts, immediately after an :undecided leadership change and an epoch 1 -> 2 transition:

    c1: layout epoch=2 ...              coordinator #PID<27104.190.0>   commit probe: :ok
    c2: layout {:error, :unavailable}   coordinator #PID<27105.191.0>   commit probe: :unavailable
    c3: layout epoch=2 ...              coordinator #PID<27104.190.0>   commit probe: :ok

One node holds its OWN coordinator pid while its peers hold the leader's; it never learns the transaction system layout and never recovers (probed 12 times over 60s). The other two are healthy, so the cluster looks fine from outside.

That matches this ticket's observation 3 -- a spurious :undecided election among healthy nodes -- and supplies a second, mechanically different reproducer for it. Notably it does NOT need a killed or crash-looping coordinator: this is three healthy nodes forming a cluster for the first time.

Possible relevance to the 'unknown mechanism' list here: bedrock-ued (a stale nil tsl_updated from an abandoned leader can blank the cached layout until the current leader's next broadcast) and bedrock-ltc (a :passive Link never registers node resources, so it is never in tsl_subscribers and its TSL cache stays nil). 'Until the next broadcast' is 'forever' if nothing re-broadcasts or re-subscribes -- which matches the never-recovers behaviour in wyo.

Also consistent with the load-dependence noted here: the chaos baseline runs 6 concurrent workers, and the failure appears at cluster formation under that load.

title: Coordinator raft leadership flaps (~1 election/s) while one coordinator is down or crash-looping at boot; one election observed with all nodes healthy
